A_target.statement:
Let $f: X \to Y$ be a [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] and $A, B \subseteq Y$.
Then:
:$\map {f^{-1} } {A \cup B} = \map {f^{-1} } A \cup \map {f^{-1} } B$
:$\map {f^{-1} } {A \cap B} = \map {f^{-1} } A \cap \map {f^{-1} } B$
:$\map {f^{-1} } {Y \setminus A} = X \setminus \map {f^{-1} } A$

B_source.statement:
Let $f: X \to Y$ be a [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] and $A, B \subseteq X$.
Then:
:$\map f {A \cup B} = \map f A \cup \map f B$
:$\map f {A \cap B} \subseteq \map f A \cap \map f B$

substitutions.the direction of the map: the reversed direction, from subsets of the codomain to subsets of the domain

derived.union is preserved by both: the one operation where the two agree
derived.intersection and complement: only contained for image, but genuinely equal for preimage

object_map.reformulation: Reverse the direction of the set map, replacing forward image by the pointwise membership condition of preimage.

validity_conditions: Preimage is defined pointwise by a membership condition on a single element, so it commutes with every Boolean operation.
Image is not pointwise in this sense: an element of the image may have several preimages, which is exactly why intersections can shrink and complements fail.
The two operations are adjoint rather than inverse, which explains the asymmetry: preimage preserves all limits and colimits of subsets, while image preserves only unions.
proof_plan:
By {{Defof|Preimage of Subset under Mapping}}:
:$x \in \map {f^{-1} } A \iff \map f x \in A$
a condition on the image of the single element $x$.

For images, $y \in \map f A \cap \map f B$ may have $y = \map f a = \map f b$ with $a \in A \setminus B$ and $b \in B \setminus A$.
Hence equality degrades to containment unless $f$ is [[Definition:Injection|injective]].

The asymmetry reflects that $f^{-1}$ is a [[Definition:Galois Connection|right adjoint]] to the direct image $f$, and right adjoints preserve all [[Definition:Infimum of Set|meets]].
{{qed}}
